flush_volumes_vector.tooltip: This vector saves required volumes to change from/to each tool used on the

flush_volumes_matrix.tooltip: This matrix describes volumes (in cubic milimetres) required to purge the

flush_multiplier.tooltip: The actual flushing volumes is equal to the flush multiplier multiplied by the flushing volumes in the table.

prime_volume.tooltip: The volume of material to prime extruder on tower.

bottom_fill_flush_layers.tooltip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, force the bottom N object layers to purge on the prime tower before printing skeleton, then walls in the configured order, then skin and surface fill. This does not change bottom shell layers.

top_fill_flush_layers.tooltip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, force the top N object layers to purge on the prime tower before printing skeleton, then walls in the configured order, then skin and surface fill. This does not change top shell layers.

skeleton_flush_slowdown_speed.tooltip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, set the speed for slowed skeleton paths after a material change. Percent values are calculated from the speed each skeleton path would normally use.

no_prime_tower_retract_restart_extra.tooltip: When the prime tower is disabled, this additional length is added to the printer or filament extra length on restart after a material change. It has no effect when the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_solid_skeleton.tooltip: Eliminates the independent prime tower when prime volume is below 10 mm³ and every filament's minimum purge on the tower is zero. The prime volume is printed into a volume-sized solid skeleton inside the model.

wipe_tower_x.tooltip: X coordinate of the left front corner of a wipe tower

wipe_tower_y.tooltip: Y coordinate of the left front corner of a wipe tower

wipe_tower_rotation_angle.tooltip: Prime tower rotation angle with respect to x-axis.

prime_tower_brim_width.tooltip: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

prime_tower_rib_wall.tooltip: When this option is checked, the prime tower will be as close to a square as possible, meaning its width will be fixed.

wipe_tower_cone_angle.tooltip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

wipe_tower_extra_spacing.tooltip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

wipe_tower_max_purge_speed.tooltip:
The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

Increasing this speed may affect the tower's stability as well as increase the force with which the nozzle collides with any blobs that may have formed on the wipe tower.

Before increasing this parameter beyond the default of 90mm/sec, make sure your printer can reliably bridge at the increased speeds and that ooze when tool changing is well controlled.

For the wipe tower external perimeters the internal perimeter speed is used regardless of this setting.

wipe_tower_filament.tooltip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

wiping_volumes_extruders.tooltip: This vector saves required volumes to change from/to each tool used on the wipe tower. These values are used to simplify creation of the full purging volumes below.

flush_into_infill.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_support.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_skeleton.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' skeleton area. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

flush_into_objects.tooltip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

wipe_tower_bridging.tooltip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

prime_tower_start_ironing.tooltip: Ironing the purge start area reduces the risk of the nozzle scraping the prime tower during subsequent printing.

prime_tower_start_offset.tooltip: Moves the start of the prime tower purge path inward along the first purge line. This keeps startup blobs inside the tower.

prime_tower_corner_rib_length.tooltip: Bottom side length of the square corner ribs on the square prime tower. The rib keeps its contact length with the wipe area and tapers outward to the blocks edges at the tower top. Set to 0 to use the perimeter line spacing.

wipe_tower_extra_flow.tooltip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

idle_temperature.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups.This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

xy_hole_compensation.tooltip: Holes of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes holes bigger. Negative value makes holes smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

xy_contour_compensation.tooltip: Contour of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes contour bigger. Negative value makes contour smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

hole_to_polyhole.tooltip:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

hole_to_polyhole_threshold.tooltip:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

thumbnails.tooltip: Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

thumbnails_format.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware

use_relative_e_distances.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option.Some extruders work better with this option unckecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked

wall_generator.tooltip: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width

wall_transition_length.tooltip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

wall_transition_filter_deviation.tooltip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

wall_transition_angle.tooltip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude

wall_distribution_count.tooltip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width

min_feature_size.tooltip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

min_length_factor.tooltip:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the ouside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visibile if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

initial_layer_min_bead_width.tooltip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

min_bead_width.tooltip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill.tooltip: This option will auto detect narrow internal solid infill area. If enabled, concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed printing up. Otherwise, rectilinear pattern is used defaultly.

mixed_color_layer_height_a.tooltip: Layer height contribution of component A for dithering virtual filaments.

mixed_color_layer_height_b.tooltip: Layer height contribution of component B for dithering virtual filaments.

mixed_filament_gradient_mode.tooltip: Enable height-weighted cadence for mixed filaments.

mixed_filament_height_lower_bound.tooltip: Lower bound used by the height-weighted mixed filament gradient mode.

mixed_filament_height_upper_bound.tooltip: Upper bound used by the height-weighted mixed filament gradient mode.

mixed_filament_advanced_dithering.tooltip: Distribute mixed filament layer-cycle cadence using an advanced ordered dithering pattern.

mixed_filament_pointillism_pixel_size.tooltip: Length of one pointillisme segment along an extrusion path.

mixed_filament_pointillism_line_gap.tooltip: Optional non-extruded spacing between adjacent pointillisme segments.

mixed_filament_surface_indentation.tooltip: XY offset applied to mixed-filament painted regions before region assignment.

dithering_z_step_size.tooltip: Layer height used in Z zones painted with dithering.

dithering_local_z_mode.tooltip: Use Variable Layers for Color Blending.

dithering_step_painted_zones_only.tooltip: When enabled, dithering Z step size is applied only where mixed filament is painted.

no_check.tooltip: Do not run validity checks such as G-code path conflict checks.

datadir.tooltip: Load settings from the given data directory.

load_custom_gcodes.tooltip: Load plate custom G-code from JSON.

zhop.tooltip: Contains z-hop present at the beginning of the custom G-code block.

position.tooltip: Position of the extruder at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code travels somewhere else, it should write to this variable so PrusaSlicer knows where it travels from when it gets control back.

e_retracted.tooltip: Retraction state at the beginning of the custom G-code block. If the custom G-code moves the extruder axis, it should write to this variable so PrusaSlicer deretracts correctly when it gets control back.

e_restart_extra.tooltip: Currently planned extra extruder priming after deretraction.

e_position.tooltip: Current position of the extruder axis. Only used with absolute extruder addressing.

current_extruder.tooltip: Zero-based index of currently used extruder.

current_object_idx.tooltip: Specific for sequential printing. Zero-based index of currently printed object.

has_wipe_tower.tooltip: Whether or not wipe tower is being generated in the print.

initial_extruder.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_tool.

initial_tool.tooltip: Zero-based index of the first extruder used in the print. Same as initial_extruder.

is_extruder_used.tooltip: Vector of bools stating whether a given extruder is used in the print.

initial_filament_type.tooltip: String containing filament type of the first used extruder.

has_single_extruder_multi_material_primi.tooltip: Are the extra multi-material priming regions used in this print?

extruded_volume.tooltip: Total filament volume extruded per extruder during the entire print.

total_toolchanges.tooltip: Number of toolchanges during the print.

extruded_volume_total.tooltip: Total volume of filament used during the entire print.

extruded_weight.tooltip: Weight per extruder extruded during the entire print. Calculated from filament_density value in Filament Settings.

extruded_weight_total.tooltip: Total weight of the print. Calculated from filament_density value in Filament Settings.

total_layer_count.tooltip: Number of layers in the entire print.

normal_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as print_time.

num_printing_extruders.tooltip: Number of extruders used during the print.

print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in normal mode (i.e. not in silent mode). Same as normal_print_time.

printing_filament_types.tooltip: Comma-separated list of all filament types used during the print.

silent_print_time.tooltip: Estimated print time when printed in silent mode.

total_cost.tooltip: Total cost of all material used in the print. Calculated from filament_cost value in Filament Settings.

total_weight.tooltip: Total weight of the print. Calculated from filament_density value in Filament Settings.

total_wipe_tower_cost.tooltip: Total cost of the material wasted on the wipe tower. Calculated from filament_cost value in Filament Settings.

total_wipe_tower_filament.tooltip: Total filament volume extruded on the wipe tower.

used_filament.tooltip: Total length of filament used in the print.

num_objects.tooltip: Total number of objects in the print.

num_instances.tooltip: Total number of object instances in the print, summed over all objects.

scale.tooltip:
Contains a string with the information about what scaling was applied to the individual objects. Indexing of the objects is zero-based (first object has index 0).
Example: 'x:100% y:50% z:100'.

input_filename_base.tooltip: Source filename of the first object, without extension.

first_layer_print_convex_hull.tooltip: Vector of points of the first layer convex hull. Each element has the following format:'[x, y]' (x and y are floating-point numbers in mm).

timestamp.tooltip: String containing current time in yyyyMMdd-hhmmss format.

print_preset.tooltip: Name of the print preset used for slicing.

filament_preset.tooltip: Names of the filament presets used for slicing. The variable is a vector containing one name for each extruder.

printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the printer preset used for slicing.

physical_printer_preset.tooltip: Name of the physical printer used for slicing.

num_extruders.tooltip: Total number of extruders, regardless of whether they are used in the current print.

layer_num.tooltip: Index of the current layer. One-based (i.e. first layer is number 1).

layer_z.tooltip: Height of the current layer above the print bed, measured to the top of the layer.

max_layer_z.tooltip: Height of the last layer above the print bed.

filament_extruder_id.tooltip: The current extruder ID. The same as current_extruder.
